annotations.text:
No new schema.

Threads = quests where type='main' (title, location, objectives → the pip row).
Last Logged = the newest sessions row (recap + events[]).
Header = progress.stories[] exactly as seeded: percent, label, telemetry, chapter.

Both tables already reach the player through useCampaign() (migration 0007, read-only). One overlay, one fetch, nothing authored twice. Every direction on the Alternates page reads the same data — only the shape varies.

Bonds = lore.relations (exact Lore-screen anatomy: 3 attitude segments, the dashed-amber 'unknown', the one sanctioned amber 'System · Bonded' row).
Arc = lore.backstory + lore.personality.

CAUTION: lore is '{}' in seed.sql, so every relation and nature string here is PLACEHOLDER, not canon. The NPC names come from the repo's own Journal dev fixture. The Flaw card shows the real unauthored state — an em dash.

The weak card, drawn honestly rather than padded.

'34 of 51 locations' is PROSE inside progress.stories[].tooltip. There is no locations table, so the only real list available is the distinct quests.location values — three of them.

Decision for you: ship this thin version, or author a locations table and derive the percent. The panel is deliberately shorter (840×520) so the thin version doesn't look broken.

Build notes

• Panel shell is LevelUpOverlay's layered frame with the player (cyan) accent, not the amber operator one.
• Scrimmed, so lib/backdropFreeze + the html[data-modal] rule already in Codex.module.css pause the sigil for free.
• Every 45° chamfer here needs the painted-diagonal recipe and a registration in chamferBorders.test.ts — the hexagon sigil needs the two-layer fix instead.
• KNOWN ISSUE: this shell is also ShopTakeover, LootTakeover, LevelUpOverlay, LootRollOverlay, ActivationSheet and PrimeSheet. It reads as 'the DM opened something for you', which a story you chose to read is not. Hence page 2.

Why these exist: the centred chamfered panel on page 1 is the app's most reused shell — six components already wear it, the shop loudest among them. Three directions that are not that, each varying a different axis. Same data in all three.

A · UNFOLDS IN PLACE — axis: space. No overlay at all.

The three cards stay on screen: the open one keeps its geometry and takes a cyan edge, the other two shrink to 0.6 and stay clickable, so switching stories never closes anything. The overview is hairlines and type on the screen's own background.

Backed by repo precedent — StartingKit's own header says route / resists modals: 'a modal that seizes it is the nagging the codex is built to avoid.'

Tradeoff: no scrim means the 640px sigil keeps turning behind the text (no backdrop-filter over moving pixels — a win), so legibility rests on the feathered dark plate under the reading column. That plate is the one thing to judge here.

B · LATTICE — axis: metaphor. The sigil stops being wallpaper.

Progress is an arc swept on the ring, threads are nodes pinned at their own angles with leaders breaking to a common gutter, the percent and chapter sit where the decorative centre used to be (the inner circles, triangles and pulse are dropped — the data lives there now).

Tradeoff, stated plainly: this is an INDEX, not a reader. One session beat fits in the lower hexagon band and 'Open Journal' carries the rest. If the overview has to hold real reading, B is the wrong direction — don't rescue it by bolting a prose panel to the side, because that panel turns back into page 1.

C · DOSSIER SPREAD — axis: typography. No frame, no scrim, no panel: three editorial columns on hairlines, and one oversized ghosted numeral (the only element of its kind in the app — keep it to one).

Note the affordance: '◀ Codex', not '✕'. This is a place you navigated to, which means it wants its own ROUTE (/codex/story/main-story) rather than overlay state on Codex.tsx. That is the real cost difference from A and B — both of those are local state — and it is also what makes C linkable and back-button-correct.

The Log column is the sessions table in full, reverse-chronological.

D · LATTICE DOSSIER — B's instrument, C's reading, joined rather than parked side by side.

The join is the leaders. Each thread's node sits on the r=220 ring at its own angle, and its leader breaks radially then runs horizontally to dock on that thread's row in the dossier column. The ring is wired into the text; move a row and its leader moves with it. That is the one thing that stops this being a radial graphic beside a prose panel — which is what the earlier advice warned would collapse back into the page-1 shell.

What each parent contributed:
• From B — the sigil promoted to instrument (progress swept as an arc, threads as nodes), and the percent + chapter sitting where the decorative centre used to be. The inner circles, triangles and pulse are dropped; the data lives there now.
• From C — hairlines instead of frames, the editorial Last Session / Log columns, and '◀ Codex' rather than '✕', so this is a route (/codex/story/main-story) and not overlay state.

Two deliberate cuts:
• The sigil is bled off the left edge at 800px. It is now the outsized element, so C's ghost numeral is GONE — one oversized thing per screen, not two.
• C's full-width footer rail is gone too: the percent is already the arc and the centre numeral, and a third readout was just noise.

The story switcher moved into the dossier's tab row — the lattice re-aims, it never closes.

Still the same data as every other direction: quests + sessions + progress.stories[]. No new schema.

E · LIVE. Click a card, click a thread — then click another node to hop straight across without surfacing.

Three depths, one continuous transform of a single body:
  Codex  -> three cards on the glyph, sigil at 0.66
  Story  -> the lattice dossier at 1.0, arc and leaders drawing on
  Thread -> 2.4x onto the node you picked, the quest record replacing the dossier

HOPPING. The other threads do not leave when you zoom — they are still pinned to the lattice, they just moved. Their positions come from the same mapping the zoom uses (P -> O + 2.4(P - O) + t), so a hop chip always sits exactly on its node. Hopping only changes which node is centred: the lattice pans, the record swaps, you never surface. Chip labels grow away from the record column so they can never land under the text.

TIMING — two clocks, not one. The entrance (arc sweep, six staggered leaders, ~2.1s) plays ONCE on mount and is allowed to be cinematic; it is a scan completing. The zoom, layer fades and focus ring fire on EVERY click and stay quick — 460 / 220 / 380ms. Hover and focus feedback (160-220ms) is fixed and scales with nothing: that is response, not choreography.
The Motion > pace tweak above the artboard scales both clocks at once, 0.5x to 2x. 1x is the tuned default. (An earlier build had these halved on a report of sluggishness that turned out to be Zen, not the timings — Chromium was always fine.)

CLIPPING. Real bug, worst exactly where it was reported. At 2.4x on the TOP node the lattice reaches 242px into the record column (46px on the middle node, 6px on the bottom). Fixed with a feathered dark ground under the record — no border, no frame, the same device direction A uses — plus text-wrap: balance on the title.

HONEST SCOPE: Main Story's three threads are wired. Character and Region open the same lattice.

SIDE QUESTS have no home. Drawn on the REAL shipped geometry this time — 1470x830, the body where the app actually puts it (y 206-762), the 640px sigil at centre (170,330), nodes on r=220, the dossier at x=520, rows 108/92. What is on these boards is buildable as drawn.

Your data, unchanged: 3 main quests have nodes; The Thicket Path, Whispers in Castella and The Mayor's Welcome have none anywhere. They only feed the Region card's location tallies.

Worth deciding first: is a side quest part of the STORY, or beside it? A and C answer that opposite ways, and B declines to answer.

A · OUTER ORBIT — your instinct, built properly. Axis: same system, lower rank.

Side nodes sit on the sigil's own outer circle (r=300) with dashed grey leaders breaking at r=315, and they get their own compact rows under a SIDE rule — 44px each, no meta line, against the main threads' 92px. Same grammar as a main thread, visibly demoted.

Tradeoff, and it is the real one: it spends the height. Three main rows plus three side rows ends at y=546 in a 556px body — it fits with 10px to spare, and a fourth of either overflows. It is also the only option where a quest gains a node without gaining importance, which is the thing you were reaching for.

B · TICKS ON THE RING — axis: presence without a claim.

A side quest is a tick across the progress ring, not a node: no leader, no row, no name until you hover one (shown hovered). They are on the instrument but not in the story — the ring says how many exist and where to click, and nothing more.

Tradeoff: unscannable. You cannot read your side quests, only discover them, and three ticks look identical until touched. Costs zero height, which is why it survives a fourth and fifth quest where A does not.

Honest wrinkle: a tick's ANGLE means nothing. The main nodes' angles are solved from their rows; these are just spaced. If that bothers you, it should — it is decoration pretending to be data.

C · OFF-LATTICE BELT — axis: honest separation.

Side quests leave the instrument entirely and sit as a labelled strip under it, in space the lattice was wasting. No ring, no wire, no rank. The centre readout moves up 56px to make room.

Tradeoff: it says out loud that these are not the story, which is either exactly right or reads as exile. It also breaks the screen's one rule — that everything on the left is the instrument — so the left half now holds two unrelated things.

Cheapest to build by a distance: no geometry at all, and it grows to 6+ quests by wrapping.
